name: 1/2" Loopie Sling (2'–4')
title: 1/2" Loopie Sling, Adjustable 2–4 ft for Rigging
meta: A 1/2" loopie sling that adjusts from 2 to 4 ft for rigging points on small to mid-size stems. Choke it, cinch it and set your block right where you want it.
tagline: Adjustable 2–4 ft rope sling for setting blocks and pulleys on smaller stems.
summary: This 1/2 inch loopie sling adjusts from about 2 to 4 feet, so one sling covers a range of stem and limb sizes when you set a rigging point. It chokes down tight and holds a block or pulley where you put it.
highlights: Adjusts from about 2 to 4 ft
1/2 in rope for light to moderate rigging
Chokes tight around the stem to resist sliding
Soft on bark compared with chain or wire
Packs small in a rigging bag

body.h: How crews use a loopie sling
p: A loopie sling is a length of hollow-braid rope with a fixed eye at one end and a bury that lets the loop slide shorter or longer. Wrap it around the stem, pass the hardware through the loop and pull it snug. The sling cinches against the bark and stays put under load, which is what you want when a block is taking the shock of a dropped piece.

The 2 to 4 foot range suits the stems most climbers rig off on removals and reductions: upper leads, smaller spars and big limbs. Because it adjusts, you are not hauling three fixed-length slings to cover the same spread.

Match the sling to the load. A 1/2 inch sling belongs on light to moderate rigging, not on heavy wood coming off a big spar. If you are unsure, step up a size and check the working load on the tag against the forces you expect, which can be many times the weight of the piece once it starts moving.

Inspect before every use: look for glazing, cut strands, a pulled bury or a stiff, crunchy section. Retire any sling that has been shock loaded hard or shows damage. Browse other adjustable rigging slings for larger diameters and longer lengths.

faq.q: What is a loopie sling used for?
faq.a: It wraps a stem or limb and chokes down to anchor a rigging block or pulley, adjusting length to fit the wood.

faq.q: Can I use a 1/2 inch loopie sling for big wood?
faq.a: No. Keep it for light to moderate loads and use a larger, higher-rated sling for heavy rigging.

name: ISC Oval Accessory Carabiner
title: ISC Oval Accessory Carabiner for Racking Gear
meta: The ISC oval accessory carabiner keeps hand saws, throw bags and spare hardware racked on your saddle. A tidy gear clip, not rated for life support or rigging.
tagline: Light oval clip for racking tools and spare hardware on your saddle.
summary: The ISC oval accessory carabiner is a simple non-locking clip for hanging gear on your saddle loops. It keeps spare pulleys, a throw bag or a pole saw cord organized so you can find them without looking.
highlights: Oval shape keeps gear centered
Non-locking gate for quick one-hand clipping
Light enough to rack several on a saddle
Accessory use only, not for life support
specs: Accessory carabiner, not for life support

p: Every climber ends up with too much hanging off the saddle. Accessory carabiners are how you keep it sorted: one for spare hardware, one for the throw bag, one for a lanyard you are not using. The oval shape lets items sit in the middle of the clip instead of sliding into a corner, and a plain gate is fast to open with a gloved hand.
Rack them on the gear loops or saddle storage points, not on your bridge or the attachment points that carry your weight.

Clip a couple to the back of the saddle for the gear you only need now and then, and keep the ones up front for what you reach for most. A simple, consistent rack means less fumbling for the right tool when you are tied in and working a limb.

An accessory carabiner is a storage clip. Do not use it to tie in, to connect a lanyard, or in a rigging system, even for a light load. Life-support connectors need to be rated for that job, locking where required, and used as the manufacturer and ANSI Z133 direct.
Because accessory and life-support carabiners can look alike, many climbers keep them in a different color so there is no mix-up mid-climb. For other gear clips see our non-locking carabiners.

faq.q: Can I climb on the ISC oval accessory carabiner?
faq.a: No. It is for racking gear only and must never be used in a life-support or rigging system.

faq.q: Why use an oval instead of a D shape for racking?
faq.a: The oval keeps items centered and lets several pieces hang side by side without crowding a corner.

name: ISC Compact Rigging Pulley (Green, Grey Wheel)
title: ISC Compact Rigging Pulley, Green with Grey Wheel
meta: The ISC compact rigging pulley gives you a light redirect for lowering lines, speed lines and lift systems. Green side plates and a grey sheave for quick ID.
tagline: Small, light rigging pulley for redirects, speed lines and lighter lowering.
summary: The ISC compact rigging pulley is a small block for redirects and lighter rigging where a full-size block is more than you need. Green side plates and a grey wheel make it easy to pick out of the bag.
highlights: Compact size for lighter rigging and redirects
Swinging side plates load mid-line
Green plates and grey sheave for fast identification
Pairs with a sling or carabiner at the anchor
specs: Opening side plates for mid-line attachment

p: Not every rigging job needs a heavy block. A compact pulley earns its place on speed lines, redirects that steer a lowering line around an obstacle, and simple lift or tensioning setups where the forces stay moderate. It is lighter to carry up and quicker to hang than a full-size block.
Open the side plates, drop the rope over the sheave and close it back up, so you can set it without threading an end. Hang it from a sling or rated connector at the anchor point.
Because it is small, it is also handy as a redirect on a lowering line that needs to clear a roof edge or fence, or as part of a simple mechanical advantage setup for tensioning a line before a cut.

Check the rating marked on the pulley and the rope diameter it is built for before you put it in a system. Remember that a redirect can see close to double the load on the line, and a dropped piece adds shock on top of that. If the job calls for catching big wood, step up to a proper rigging block.
Inspect the sheave for grooves or rough spots and the side plates for bending before each job. See the full range of rigging blocks for heavier work.

faq.q: Can I use the ISC compact pulley as a main rigging block?
faq.a: Only for light loads within its rating. For catching heavy wood, use a full-size rigging block.

faq.q: Why the green and grey colors?
faq.a: Color coding helps crews grab the right size pulley out of the bag quickly.

name: Teufelberger Epicord 10mm Sewn Eye-to-Eye Prusik
title: Teufelberger Epicord 10mm Sewn Eye-to-Eye Prusik
meta: Teufelberger Epicord 10mm sewn eye-to-eye prusik for friction hitches on MRS and SRS climbing systems. Sewn eyes, firm hand and a cover built to take heat.
tagline: Sewn 10 mm hitch cord for climbers who want a consistent, grabby friction hitch.
summary: Teufelberger Epicord is a 10 mm hitch cord, and this version comes with sewn eyes on both ends so it is ready to tie into a Distel, VT or similar friction hitch. It is a common pick for climbers running 11 to 13 mm climbing lines.
highlights: 10 mm hitch cord from Teufelberger
Factory-sewn eyes, no knots to dress
Sits low and tight for short hitch length
Works with common MRS and SRS hitches

p: A sewn eye-to-eye removes the bulk of tied terminations, so the hitch can sit closer to the micro pulley and you get more usable advance with each tend. The eyes are consistent from cord to cord, which makes it easier to repeat a hitch you like.

Epicord is a firm, purpose-built hitch cord. Paired with the right climbing line it grabs reliably and releases smoothly, which is what you want when you are descending through a canopy with a saw on your hip.

Hitch behavior depends on the combination of cord and climbing line, the hitch you tie and how many wraps you use. Always test a new setup low and slow before you trust it at height, and confirm the climbing line diameter is within the range Teufelberger recommends for this cord.

Hitch cord is a wear item. Retire it when the cover is glazed, fuzzed through or stiff, or when the sewn eyes show any damage. Look over all our eye-and-eye prusiks if you need a different diameter or length.
Many climbers keep two sewn eye-to-eyes in the kit: one on the rope and a spare in the bag, so a glazed hitch can be swapped on the spot instead of ending the climb early.

faq.q: What hitch should I tie with Epicord 10mm?
faq.a: Climbers commonly use the Distel or VT. Use the hitch you are trained on and test it on your climbing line before climbing.

faq.q: How often should I replace a sewn eye-to-eye?
faq.a: Replace it as soon as the cover is glazed or worn through, the eyes are damaged, or it has been heat-damaged.

name: Teufelberger Sirius 20mm Bull Rope
title: Teufelberger Sirius 20mm Bull Rope for Heavy Rigging
meta: Teufelberger Sirius 20mm bull rope for heavy removals and big-wood rigging. A thick rigging line that handles well through blocks and lowering devices.
tagline: Big-diameter bull rope for heavy removals and catching large wood.
summary: The Teufelberger Sirius 20mm bull rope is a heavy rigging line for removals where you are lowering big wood through a block and lowering device. At about 3/4 inch, it is sized for the loads a crew sees when spars and large limbs come down.
highlights: 20 mm (about 3/4 in) diameter for heavy rigging
Made for blocks, port-a-wraps and other lowering devices
Firm braid that resists flattening under load
Typical price shown for a common working length; check the listing

body.h: When you need a bull rope
p: Lowering lines get sized to the wood. When the job is dropping big tops, heavy limbs or spar sections into a block, a 1/2 or 5/8 inch line runs out of margin quickly. A 20 mm bull rope gives the crew the strength and the hand they need to catch and control those loads with a friction device at the base.
Thicker rope also wears better over hundreds of cycles through a block, and it is easier for the ground person to hold and run under tension.

A bull rope also gives the ground crew more control. With the right number of wraps on the lowering device, they can let a heavy piece run and then stop it smoothly, instead of fighting a thin line that bites into their gloves.

Plan every rig from the forces, not the weight of the piece. A dropped load can shock a system with several times its weight. Check that every component, from sling and block to lowering device and anchor tree, is rated for the job, and keep the rope within its working load limit.
Inspect the rope before each job for cuts, glazing, crushed sections and core damage, and retire it if in doubt. Store it clean and dry in a bag. Compare other rigging rope options for lighter work.

faq.q: What size is a 20mm bull rope in inches?
faq.a: 20 mm is about 3/4 inch.

faq.q: Do I need a 20mm rope for most rigging?
faq.a: No. It is for heavy removals and big wood. Lighter jobs are usually rigged on 1/2 to 5/8 inch line.

name: Configuration Aids and Corner Traps
title: Carabiner Configuration Aids and Corner Traps
meta: Carabiner configuration aids and corner traps hold a carabiner in position on a pulley, ring or device so your system stays oriented and loads the spine.
tagline: Rubber keepers that hold carabiners in place so your system stays oriented.
summary: A carabiner corner trap, or configuration aid, is a small keeper that holds a carabiner in position on a pulley, ring or device. It keeps the connector from rotating so the load stays on the spine and your setup stays tidy.
highlights: Holds a carabiner in a fixed position
Helps keep loads on the spine, not the gate
Keeps hitch and pulley setups from flopping around
Light, cheap and easy to fit
specs: Most arborist carabiners; check fit for your connector

p: Carabiners like to rotate. On a micro pulley, a ring or a mechanical device, a connector that flips can end up cross-loaded or pressing on its gate. A corner trap holds the carabiner in the right orientation so the spine takes the load and the system sits the same way each time you clip in.
They also make hitch setups easier to manage. With the pulley carabiner held in place, the tender works smoothly and nothing twists when you change direction in the tree.

Fit the keeper so it captures the carabiner without blocking the gate from opening and closing fully. A gate that cannot lock is a bigger problem than a carabiner that rotates. Check the fit with the gloves you climb in.

Configuration aids do not carry load and do not replace a properly rated, locking connector. Inspect them for splits and replace when they stop holding firmly. Browse all carabiners and hardware for connectors that suit your setup.

They are inexpensive enough to keep a few spares in the kit bag. When one tears or loses its grip, swap it at the truck rather than trying to make do in the tree, where a loose carabiner can turn a smooth system into a fight.

faq.q: Do corner traps carry any load?
faq.a: No. They only hold the carabiner in position. The carabiner and device do the work.

faq.q: Will a corner trap fit any carabiner?
faq.a: Most arborist carabiners, but check that the gate still opens and locks fully once it is fitted.

name: ISC Offset Oval Quadlock Carabiner
title: ISC Offset Oval Quadlock Carabiner
meta: The ISC offset oval Quadlock carabiner adds a four-action auto-locking gate to an offset oval shape for climbing systems, hitch setups and secure connections.
tagline: Offset oval with a four-action gate for connections that must stay shut.
summary: The ISC offset oval Quadlock carabiner pairs its offset oval body with a four-action auto-locking gate. The extra action makes it harder for rope or branches to roll the gate open, which is why climbers pick it for key connections on their saddle.
highlights: Quadlock four-action auto-locking gate
Offset oval shape for good gate opening
Resists accidental opening against rope and limbs
Suited to bridge, lanyard and hitch connections

p: A standard triple-action gate opens with a slide, a twist and a push. A Quadlock adds one more step, so the gate is much less likely to be opened by a rope running across it or a limb catching it while you move through the tree. For connectors that hold you, many climbers think that extra margin is worth the small extra effort.
The offset oval shape gives good gate clearance while still letting rope and hardware sit naturally on the spine.

Common spots for a Quadlock are the bridge connection, the lanyard end and the connection to a friction device, where a gate rolling open would be serious. For gear that clips and unclips all day, some climbers keep a quicker triple-action carabiner instead.

Practice the gate on the ground with your work gloves until it is second nature, especially if you are used to triple-action carabiners. Load it along the spine with the gate closed and locked, and keep it out of positions where it can be cross-loaded over an edge.

As life-support equipment, it should be used per ISC's instructions and ANSI Z133, inspected before each climb and retired after a big fall or any damage. See all auto-locking carabiners for more shapes.

faq.q: What is a Quadlock carabiner?
faq.a: It is ISC's four-action auto-locking gate, which takes four separate movements to open.

faq.q: Is a Quadlock harder to use with gloves?
faq.a: It takes some practice. Most climbers get comfortable after working it on the ground for a few minutes.

name: Husqvarna 360BT Backpack Blower
title: Husqvarna 360BT Backpack Blower: Specs and Uses
meta: The Husqvarna 360BT backpack blower has a 65.6 cc X-Torq engine for clearing sawdust, leaves and chip debris after tree work. Specs, uses and care tips.
tagline: High-output gas backpack blower for fast cleanup after tree jobs.
summary: The Husqvarna 360BT is a gas backpack blower with a 65.6 cc X-Torq engine, built for crews that need to clear a big site quickly. After a removal it moves sawdust, leaves and chip spray off lawns, drives and roofs fast.
highlights: 65.6 cc X-Torq two-stroke engine
Backpack frame with padded harness for long cleanups
Cruise control style throttle setting
Strong airflow for wet leaves and packed debris
Common choice for tree and landscape crews

body.h: Cleanup is part of the job
p: The customer judges the job by how the yard looks when you leave. After rigging down a tree and chipping the brush, there is sawdust in the grass, leaves on the drive and chip spray in the beds. The Husqvarna 360BT has the output to push that debris into piles quickly, even when it is damp.
As a backpack unit, the weight rides on your shoulders and hips instead of your arm, which matters when cleanup takes half an hour on a big site.

Run fresh, properly mixed two-stroke fuel and keep the air filter clean, since a blower pulls in a lot of dust. Check the harness and tube clamps regularly. Wear hearing and eye protection, and keep the nozzle pointed away from people, cars and windows.
At the end of the season, run the carburetor dry or use stabilized fuel to avoid gumming. See other blowers and power equipment for jobsite cleanup.

Fit the harness so the weight sits on your hips, and set the tube length so the nozzle rides low and points ahead of you. Working with the wind and moving debris in stages, toward the chipper or a tarp, saves time and keeps the job looking tidy when the customer walks out.

faq.q: What engine does the Husqvarna 360BT have?
faq.a: It has a 65.6 cc X-Torq two-stroke engine.

faq.q: Is the 360BT good for wet leaves?
faq.a: Yes. It is a high-output model that handles damp leaves and packed debris better than smaller handheld blowers.

name: Jameson 6'–12' Telescoping Pole
title: Jameson Telescoping Pole, 6–12 ft Fiberglass
meta: The Jameson telescoping pole extends from 6 to 12 ft, a fiberglass handle for pole saw heads and pruners. Extend it for reach and collapse it to carry.
tagline: Fiberglass pole that extends from 6 to 12 ft for pole saw and pruner heads.
summary: The Jameson telescoping pole extends from about 6 to 12 feet, so one handle covers low clearance pruning and higher limbs. It takes Jameson pole saw heads and pruners and collapses short for the truck.
highlights: Extends from about 6 to 12 ft
Fiberglass construction
Accepts Jameson pole saw and pruner heads
Locks at working length
Collapses short for transport
specs: about 6 ft collapsed to 12 ft extended
Jameson pole saw and pruner heads

p: Clearance pruning over sidewalks and drives, raising canopies and taking out deadwood from the ground all call for different reach. A telescoping pole lets you work at 6 feet for low limbs and run it out toward 12 when you need it, without swapping poles.
Fiberglass gives a stiff handle that tracks the saw stroke well, and it is the material pole tools have used for decades on tree and grounds crews.

A telescoping pole also keeps the truck rack simpler. Instead of carrying a short pole for low work and a long one for higher limbs, one adjustable handle covers both, and it fits easier in a compartment when collapsed. Pair it with a sharp pole saw head and a pruner head and most ground pruning is covered.

Do not assume any pole is safe near energized lines. Only qualified line-clearance workers should prune near power lines, with dielectric-tested tools and the minimum approach distances set by ANSI Z133 and OSHA. Keep the pole clean and dry and inspect it for cracks or damage.
Check the locking collar each time you extend the pole so a section cannot slip under load, and wear eye protection and a helmet when cutting overhead. Browse more poles and kits for other lengths.

faq.q: What heads fit the Jameson telescoping pole?
faq.a: It is built for Jameson pole saw and pruner heads. Check the fitting style before mixing brands.

faq.q: Can I use it near power lines?
faq.a: Only if you are a qualified line-clearance worker using tools tested for that work and following required approach distances.

name: Husqvarna 522L Professional String Trimmer
title: Husqvarna 522L Professional String Trimmer
meta: The Husqvarna 522L is a professional straight-shaft string trimmer with a 21.7 cc X-Torq engine for trimming around stumps, fences and jobsite edges.
tagline: Light, pro-grade straight-shaft trimmer for edges, stumps and site cleanup.
summary: The Husqvarna 522L is a professional string trimmer with a 21.7 cc X-Torq engine and a straight shaft. Tree crews use it to knock down grass around stumps and fences and tidy edges after a removal.
highlights: 21.7 cc X-Torq two-stroke engine
Straight shaft for reach under shrubs and fences
Professional build for daily use
Light enough to run one-handed for short bursts

body.h: Why a tree crew carries a trimmer
p: After a stump grind or removal, the area around the work zone often needs tidying: grass growing up around a stump, weeds along a fence where brush was dragged, or long grass around a landing zone. A light trimmer handles that in minutes and leaves the site looking finished.
The straight shaft gets under shrubs, along fence lines and around obstacles more easily than a curved shaft, and the X-Torq engine is built to run cleaner and use less fuel.

It is also useful for clearing tall grass and weeds out of a drop zone before the work starts, so the ground crew can see trip hazards and the brush is easier to drag. A professional-grade trimmer handles daily use without the plastic wear points that wear out consumer units.

Use fresh two-stroke mix at the ratio Husqvarna specifies, keep the air filter clean and replace trimmer line with the size the head is designed for. Wear eye protection and hearing protection, and keep bystanders well back since debris flies.
Clean grass off the head and shaft after each use. Find other blowers and power equipment for jobsite cleanup.
Tap-feed heads make it quick to advance line, and keeping a spare spool in the truck means a broken line does not end the job early.

faq.q: What engine does the Husqvarna 522L have?
faq.a: A 21.7 cc X-Torq two-stroke engine.

faq.q: Is the 522L straight shaft or curved?
faq.a: It has a straight shaft.

name: ANSI Gate-Rated Steel Snap Hook
title: ANSI Gate-Rated Steel Snap Hook for Lanyards
meta: A double-locking steel snap hook with an ANSI gate rating for lanyards and fliplines. Tough, simple and easy to clip with gloves on when you are in the tree.
tagline: Double-locking steel snap with a gate rated to current ANSI requirements.
summary: This steel snap hook has a double-locking keeper and a gate rated to the strength current ANSI rules require for snap hooks. It is a durable choice for building or replacing a hook on a lanyard or flipline.
highlights: Steel body for wear resistance
Double-locking (two-action) keeper
Gate rated to current ANSI snap hook requirements
Easy to work with gloved hands

p: Older snap hooks could be rolled open if the gate was pressed hard against a ring or anchor. Gate-rated snaps are built so the keeper holds against a much higher side load, which closes off that failure. Arborists who use snap hooks on lanyards and fliplines should be using gate-rated hardware.
Steel stands up to the abrasion that comes with working around bark and spurs all day.

Many climbers prefer a snap hook on a flipline because it is quick to clip to a saddle D-ring with one hand, and the narrow nose sits neatly in the ring. The steel snap also takes wear from contact with spurs and rough bark better than aluminum hardware does.

A snap hook on a lanyard is life support. It should be attached by a qualified splicer or with a termination the manufacturer approves, and the lanyard should meet ANSI Z133 and the maker's instructions. Do not tie a snap onto a rope with a knot unless that knot is part of an approved system.
Check the keeper springs closed and locks every time, look for cracks, rust or burrs, and retire the hook after a fall or if it is damaged. See other snap hooks for different sizes.

faq.q: What does ANSI gate-rated mean on a snap hook?
faq.a: It means the gate is built to resist the side load current ANSI standards require, so it is much harder to force open.

faq.q: Can I use a snap hook for climbing?
faq.a: Yes, on lanyards and fliplines when it is properly attached and rated. Follow ANSI Z133 and the maker's instructions.

name: 4' Eye-to-Eye Webbing Sling
title: 4 ft Eye-to-Eye Webbing Sling for Crane Rigging
meta: A 4 ft eye-to-eye webbing sling for crane picks and general rigging. Flat polyester webbing grips the stem and spreads load across the bark.
tagline: Flat 4 ft webbing sling for crane picks, chokers and general rigging.
summary: A 4 foot eye-to-eye webbing sling is a flat sling with a sewn eye at each end. Crews use it as a choker on crane picks and as an anchor sling for blocks on smaller stems.
highlights: 4 ft length with sewn eyes both ends
Flat webbing spreads load over the bark
Works as choker, basket or vertical hitch
Light and easy to stack in the truck

body.h: Using webbing slings on tree work
p: Flat webbing has a wide footprint, so it grips the stem and is gentler on bark than chain or wire. On crane removals, slings choke each pick and connect to the hook. On conventional rigging they make quick anchors for a block or a lowering device.
A 4 foot sling fits smaller picks and stems. For big wood you may need longer slings, wider webbing or a basket hitch to get the capacity.

Webbing slings stack flat and weigh little, so a crew can bring several lengths on every job. The 4 foot size is often used in pairs or as a short choker on smaller limbs, and it is easy to tell apart from longer slings in the bag by color or tag.

Read the tag. Webbing slings are rated by hitch type, and a choker hitch carries less than a vertical or basket hitch. On a crane pick, the sling capacity has to match the actual weight plus the dynamic load, and that is the crane operator and rigger's call together.
Remove any sling from service with cuts, burns, holes, broken stitching, chemical damage or a missing tag. Keep slings away from the chainsaw cut. Browse more crane slings for longer lengths.

faq.q: What is an eye-to-eye sling used for?
faq.a: It connects loads to a crane hook or anchors rigging gear, used as a choker, basket or vertical hitch.

faq.q: Does the choker hitch reduce capacity?
faq.a: Yes. Check the tag for the choker rating, which is lower than the vertical rating.

name: Rig Guy Wire Stop 4-Way Hub
title: Rig Guy Wire Stop 4-Way Hub for Cabling Systems
meta: The Rig Guy Wire Stop 4-way hub joins up to four cable runs at a central point for multi-lead tree cabling and guying layouts. Check fit with your cable size.
tagline: Central hub that joins up to four cable runs in multi-lead cabling layouts.
summary: The Rig Guy Wire Stop 4-way hub joins up to four cable runs at one point, which is how arborists build hub-and-spoke cabling layouts on trees with several leads. It works with the Wire Stop termination system.
highlights: Connects up to four cable runs
For hub-and-spoke multi-lead cabling
Part of the Rig Guy Wire Stop system
Keeps cable runs organized at the center

body.h: When a hub layout makes sense
p: On trees with three or more weak or codominant leads, a hub layout ties several leads to a central point so the load is shared rather than stacked on one cable. It also cuts down on the number of cable runs crossing the canopy compared with running every lead to every other one.
A hub like this keeps those runs together in one fitting, which is cleaner to install and easier to inspect later.

Hub layouts are common on large multi-stem trees such as silver maples, elms and oaks where several leads grow from a single union. The hub lets the arborist design the system around the tree's structure instead of forcing every cable through a single crotch.

Cabling should be designed and installed by a qualified arborist following ANSI A300 supplemental support practices. That covers cable size, hardware rating, anchor placement and how high in the crown the system goes. Match the hub to the cable type and size it is built for, and use only compatible terminations.
Schedule inspections after storms and at regular intervals, and record the hardware used. See our full cabling hardware range for anchors and terminations.

faq.q: How many cables does the 4-way hub take?
faq.a: Up to four cable runs.

faq.q: Who should install a cabling hub system?
faq.a: A qualified arborist following ANSI A300 cabling practices.

name: One-Man Vinyl Bucket Truck Cover with Foam Insert
title: One-Man Vinyl Bucket Truck Cover with Foam Insert
h1: One-Man Vinyl Bucket Truck Cover with Foam Insert
meta: A one-man vinyl bucket truck cover with a foam insert keeps rain, snow and debris out of the bucket when parked. Sheds water and helps the bucket stay dry.
tagline: Vinyl cover with a foam insert that keeps a one-man bucket dry and clean.
summary: This bucket truck cover fits a one-man bucket and uses a foam insert to crown the top so rain and snow run off. It keeps water, leaves and sawdust out of the bucket when the truck sits overnight or between jobs.
highlights: Fits one-man aerial lift buckets
Heavy vinyl sheds rain and snow
Foam insert crowns the cover so water runs off
Keeps leaves and sawdust out of the bucket

p: An open bucket collects rain, snow, leaves and sawdust. Standing water in a bucket liner is a problem for the liner and for anyone who climbs in the next morning, and debris can foul controls. A fitted cover keeps it clean and dry between jobs.
The foam insert lifts the center of the cover so water runs off instead of pooling and stretching the vinyl.

A covered bucket is also nicer to step into on a cold morning. There is no puddle to stand in, no wet leaves underfoot and no grit on the floor that can work into the liner or onto controls. For crews that park trucks outside overnight, a cover pays for itself quickly in cleanup time saved.
Measure the top of your bucket before ordering, since one-man buckets vary between manufacturers. Remove the cover before operating the boom and stow it where it cannot blow into traffic.

A cover does not replace inspection of the bucket and liner. Insulated buckets and liners on line-clearance trucks need their own testing and inspection. Wipe the vinyl clean and let it dry before folding. Shop other bucket truck accessories.
Store the cover in a dry compartment when it is not on the bucket so the vinyl does not crack or mildew.

faq.q: Will this cover fit a two-man bucket?
faq.a: No. It is sized for a one-man bucket. Check your bucket's dimensions before ordering.

faq.q: What does the foam insert do?
faq.a: It crowns the cover so rain and snow run off instead of pooling.

name: ISC Squirrel Tether Kit
title: ISC Squirrel Tether Kit for SRS Climbing Systems
meta: The ISC Squirrel tether kit is a replacement or spare tether for ISC's SRS climbing setup. Inspect and replace tethers as part of routine SRS system care.
tagline: Replacement tether kit for ISC's SRS system.
summary: The ISC Squirrel tether kit is a replacement tether for ISC's SRS setup, used to connect the device into the climbing system. Tethers are a wear part, and keeping a spare means a worn one does not end your climbing day.
highlights: Replacement tether for ISC's SRS setup
Keeps the device connected correctly in the system
Swap when worn instead of replacing the whole device
Made by ISC for its own hardware

p: In an SRS setup, the tether links the device to the rest of the system at the right spacing so the hitch and device work together as designed. It sees constant flexing and abrasion, and it is often the first part to show wear.
Replacing the tether with the maker's own kit keeps the geometry and strength the way ISC intended.

Keeping a spare tether in the kit bag is cheap insurance. A tether can wear through on rough bark or get nicked by a saw, and having a replacement at the truck means the climber can swap it and keep working instead of shutting the climb down for the day.

Install it exactly as ISC's instructions show, and confirm the kit is listed for your device before you buy. Do not substitute homemade tethers or cord. Have a competent person check the setup, and test it low before you climb.

Inspect the tether before each climb for fuzzing, cuts, glazing and worn stitching, and retire it at the first sign of damage. SRS climbing requires training and gear used per ANSI Z133 and manufacturer instructions. See more SRS devices.

faq.q: How do I know the Squirrel tether kit fits my device?
faq.a: Check ISC's compatibility listing for the kit before buying and install it per their instructions.

faq.q: When should I replace the tether?
faq.a: At the first sign of cuts, glazing, heavy fuzzing or worn stitching.

name: Petzl RAY 12mm Fall Arrest Rope
title: Petzl RAY 12mm Low-Stretch Fall Arrest Rope
meta: Petzl RAY 12mm is a low-stretch kernmantle rope for fall arrest backup lines and rope access. Used with mobile fall arresters such as the Petzl ASAP.
tagline: 12 mm low-stretch kernmantle rope for fall arrest backup lines.
summary: The Petzl RAY 12mm is a low-stretch kernmantle rope made for fall arrest backup lines, where it runs through a mobile fall arrester. Arborists and rope access workers use it as the safety line in two-rope systems.
highlights: 12 mm low-stretch kernmantle construction
Made for use with Petzl mobile fall arresters
Firm handling for backup and safety lines
Sold in set lengths, often with a sewn termination

p: In two-rope work, one line carries the climber and the second is a backup that catches a fall if the main line or anchor fails. The RAY is built for that backup role: a 12 mm low-stretch rope that works with mobile fall arresters such as the Petzl ASAP, which follow you up and down the line and lock if you fall.
In tree work it shows up on removals with a second tie-in, in utility and rope access, and on crews that run formal two-rope systems.

Fall arrest systems are tested as a set. Use the RAY with the devices Petzl lists as compatible for that diameter, and follow their instructions for anchors, terminations and clearance. Fall arrest work requires training and gear that meets the applicable standard.
Inspect before every use, keep it out of chainsaw reach and away from chemicals, and retire it after a significant fall or damage. Compare other static climbing rope.

The RAY is often sold in set lengths, sometimes with a sewn termination on one end. Choose a length that reaches the ground from your highest anchor with extra to spare, and mark or tag each rope so you can track its history and age.

faq.q: What device works with the Petzl RAY 12mm?
faq.a: Petzl mobile fall arresters such as the ASAP. Check Petzl's compatibility chart for your device.

faq.q: Is the RAY a dynamic rope?
faq.a: No. It is a low-stretch kernmantle rope.

name: ISC Twister Swivel Eye Carabiner
title: ISC Twister Swivel Eye Carabiner, Auto-Locking
meta: The ISC Twister swivel eye carabiner has a built-in swivel so ropes and lanyards don't twist. An auto-locking connector for climbing systems and rigging setups.
tagline: Auto-locking carabiner with a built-in swivel eye to keep lines from twisting.
summary: The ISC Twister swivel eye carabiner is an auto-locking carabiner with a swivel built into a captive eye. It lets a rope or lanyard spin freely, so you get less twist in your system without adding a separate swivel.
highlights: Built-in swivel eye
Auto-locking gate
Reduces twist in ropes and lanyards
One connector instead of carabiner plus swivel

p: Rope twist builds up as you move around the tree and can kink a lanyard or wind up a climbing line. A swivel lets the connection rotate so the twist bleeds out. The Twister puts that swivel right in the carabiner, which saves a link in the system and keeps things compact.
Climbers use it on lanyard ends, at the bottom of an SRS system or anywhere a line needs to spin freely.

The swivel also helps when a lanyard needs to rotate as you move around the stem, and it keeps a climbing line from transferring twist into a friction device. That means smoother tending and less fiddling to untwist a line between climbs.

Load the carabiner along its long axis, and make sure the swivel turns freely before each use. Keep it clean of sap and grit, which can stiffen the swivel. As life-support hardware it must be used to ISC's instructions and ANSI Z133, inspected before every climb and retired after a fall or any damage.
Check that the swivel eye is suited to the rope or termination you attach, since sharp edges or poor fit can damage a splice. See all auto-locking carabiners.

faq.q: What does the swivel on the ISC Twister do?
faq.a: It lets the attached rope or lanyard rotate so twists do not build up.

faq.q: Can I use it in an SRS system?
faq.a: Many climbers do. Follow ISC's instructions and check compatibility with your setup.

name: Buckingham Dyneema 7' Flipline Connection Strap
title: Buckingham Dyneema 7 ft Flipline Connection Strap
h1: Buckingham Dyneema 7 ft Flipline Connection Strap
meta: The Buckingham Dyneema 7 ft flipline connection strap is a strong, light strap used with fliplines and rope grabs. Check rating and compatibility before use.
tagline: Light 7 ft Dyneema strap used with fliplines and rope grabs.
summary: The Buckingham Dyneema 7 ft flipline connection strap is a light, strong strap used in flipline and rope grab setups. Dyneema keeps the weight down and resists stretch.
highlights: 7 ft length
Dyneema construction for strength and low weight
Made by Buckingham
For use with fliplines and rope grabs

p: Buckingham makes this strap for flipline setups, where a connection between the saddle, the flipline and a rope grab or adjuster has to be strong and light. Dyneema is very strong for its weight and stretches very little, which makes it a good material for straps that carry load without adding bulk.
The 7 foot length gives room to work around larger stems and in setups where a longer connection is needed.

Many climbers run a strap like this when they need a long, light connection that will not soak up water or stretch under load. It also packs small and weighs very little on the saddle, which matters on long removals where every ounce adds up over the day.

Dyneema has a low melting point, so keep it away from friction heat. Do not tie it in knots or use it where a friction hitch rubs on it. Use the strap only in the way Buckingham specifies for your flipline and rope grab, and with rated connectors.

Inspect before every use for cuts, abrasion, discoloration and broken stitching. Lanyards and fliplines are life-support gear and must meet ANSI Z133 and be used by trained climbers. See other rope grabs.

faq.q: How long is the Buckingham flipline strap?
faq.a: It is 7 feet long.

faq.q: Can Dyneema be used with friction hitches?
faq.a: No. Dyneema has a low melting point and should not be used where friction heat builds up.

name: Yale Scandere 11.7mm Static Climbing Rope (Yellow/Gray)
title: Yale Scandere 11.7mm Static Climbing Rope
meta: Yale Scandere 11.7mm static climbing rope in yellow and gray. A low-stretch arborist line for SRS and MRS that works well with friction hitches and devices.
tagline: Low-stretch 11.7 mm arborist climbing line for SRS and MRS.
summary: Yale Scandere is an 11.7 mm low-stretch climbing rope built for arborists, shown here in yellow and gray. It suits SRS ascents, where stretch wastes effort, and works with common hitches and mechanical devices.
highlights: 11.7 mm diameter
Low stretch for efficient SRS ascents
Works with friction hitches and many mechanical devices
Yellow/gray color for visibility in the canopy

p: On SRS, every inch of stretch is effort you spend before you go up. A low-stretch line like Scandere moves you up the tree with each step, and it also gives a firm feel when you work positioned in the canopy. Many climbers run it for both SRS and MRS.
At 11.7 mm it sits in the range most arborist hitches and devices are built for. Always confirm your device lists 11.7 mm rope.

The yellow and gray color pattern makes it easy to spot in the canopy and tell apart from other ropes on the job, which helps when more than one climber is in the tree. Many climbers also like that a firm, round rope runs predictably through hitches and devices over the life of the line.

Climbing rope is life support. Use it to Yale's instructions and ANSI Z133, inspect it before every climb, and retire it if you find cuts, core damage, glazing or flat spots. Keep it bagged and away from saw chain, fuel and battery acid.
Wash it as Yale recommends and let it dry out of the sun. A new rope can feel stiff at first and loosen up with use. Compare more static climbing rope.

faq.q: Is Yale Scandere good for SRS?
faq.a: Yes. Its low stretch makes it a common SRS choice, as long as your device is rated for 11.7 mm.

faq.q: What diameter is Scandere?

name: Husqvarna Starter Pawl for 372XP and 390XP Chainsaws
title: Husqvarna Starter Pawl for 372XP and 390XP Saws
meta: Replacement Husqvarna starter pawl for 372XP and 390XP chainsaws. Fix a starter that spins without catching the flywheel and get the saw back on the job.
tagline: OEM-style starter pawl for 372XP and 390XP saws that won't catch on the pull.
summary: This Husqvarna starter pawl fits the 372XP and 390XP chainsaws. If the starter rope pulls but the engine does not turn, a worn or broken pawl is a common cause and an easy fix.
highlights: Fits Husqvarna 372XP and 390XP
Restores starter engagement with the flywheel
Cheap fix for a common wear part
Keep a spare in the saw kit

p: The pawls are small spring-loaded catches on the flywheel side that the starter pulley grabs when you pull the cord. When they wear, break or stick with gunk, the starter spins freely and the engine does not turn over. Big saws like the 372XP and 390XP put a lot of load on them, so they do wear.
Before replacing, check that the pawl is not just stuck with sawdust and oil. If it is rounded off, cracked or missing, replace it, and the spring if needed.

Keeping a couple of pawls and springs in the saw kit is cheap insurance on big saws that see daily use. A spare pawl takes minutes to fit at the truck and can save a trip back to the shop or a dealer visit in the middle of a job.

Remove the starter cover, clean the area and inspect the flywheel. Fit the new pawl and spring so it moves freely and returns. Reinstall the starter and pull gently to check it catches before starting the saw.
If you are not comfortable working on the saw, have a dealer do it. Always run the saw with chaps, eye and hearing protection, and a helmet. See other power equipment parts.

faq.q: Does this pawl fit the 372XP and 390XP?
faq.a: Yes, it is listed for both. Check your saw model before ordering.

faq.q: Why does my starter rope pull but the saw won't turn?
faq.a: A worn, broken or stuck starter pawl is a common cause.

name: ISC Big Dan Steel Carabiner with Triple-Action Gate
title: ISC Big Dan Steel Carabiner, Triple-Action Gate
meta: The ISC Big Dan is a large steel carabiner with a triple-action auto-locking gate. Wide opening for anchors, rigging rings and bulky hardware on the job.
tagline: Large steel carabiner with a wide opening and triple-action locking gate.
summary: The ISC Big Dan steel carabiner is a large connector with a triple-action auto-locking gate. Its size and wide opening make it easy to clip around bulky hardware, rigging rings or thick slings.
highlights: Steel construction for durability
Triple-action auto-locking gate
Large size and wide gate opening
Handles bulky hardware and thick slings

p: Sometimes a standard carabiner just will not fit around what you need to clip: a big rigging ring, a thick sling, or two pieces of hardware at once. The Big Dan has the room, and steel stands up to the abrasion and knocks that come with rigging and anchor work.
The triple-action gate locks itself when it closes, so you are not relying on remembering to screw a sleeve down.

Crews often use it at anchors and on rigging setups, where they need to clip a large ring, a thick sling or a bundle of hardware without fighting for space. It is heavier than an aluminum carabiner, so most climbers keep it on the rigging rack rather than on the saddle.

Load it along the spine, gate closed and locked. Large carabiners can be more prone to cross-loading if something sits in the nose, so check orientation when it is under load. Check the strength markings on the carabiner match what your system needs.

Inspect for cracks, burrs and gate function, and retire after a big fall or damage. Life-support use requires training and use per ANSI Z133 and ISC's instructions. Browse other auto-locking carabiners.
Steel resists grooving from rope and wear from sling contact better than aluminum, so a Big Dan used on rigging usually outlasts a lighter connector in the same job.

faq.q: What is the ISC Big Dan used for?
faq.a: Clipping bulky hardware, big rings and thick slings where a standard carabiner is too small.

faq.q: Is the Big Dan auto-locking?
faq.a: Yes. It has a triple-action auto-locking gate.

name: DMM XS Impact Block
title: DMM XS Impact Block for Light Rigging
meta: The DMM XS Impact Block is the smallest in DMM's Impact range, made for lighter rigging and redirects where a big block is overkill. Check rating and rope size.
tagline: Smallest block in DMM's Impact line, for light rigging and redirects.
summary: The DMM XS Impact Block is the smallest size in DMM's Impact Block range, made for lighter arborist rigging. It gives you a proper rigging block for small wood and redirects without the weight of a full-size block.
highlights: Smallest size in the DMM Impact Block range
Made for arborist rigging loads
Opening side plates for mid-line loading
Light enough to carry on the saddle

p: Most rigging does not involve giant wood. Pruning, reductions and smaller removals need a block to control limbs and tops, and a smaller block is easier to set and carry. The XS gives you DMM's Impact design in a size suited to those jobs.
It also works well as a redirect or as a second block in a system to steer a lowering line.

The smaller size also makes it easier to set from the climbing position. Hang it from a sling or rated connector, drop the lowering line over the sheave and close the plates, then let the ground crew take the load through a friction device at the base. For crews that rig small wood often, a block this size quickly becomes the one that goes up on most climbs.

Read the ratings marked on the block and match rope diameter to what it is built for. Rigging forces rise quickly when a piece drops, so plan your cuts to keep shock loads within the block's working limits. For heavy wood, step up to a larger block.
Inspect the sheave, axle and side plates before each job. Retire the block if it has been overloaded or deformed. See all rigging blocks.

faq.q: Is the DMM XS Impact Block for heavy rigging?
faq.a: No. It is the smallest in the range, for lighter rigging and redirects.

faq.q: What rope works in the XS Impact Block?
faq.a: Check DMM's marked rope diameter range for the block before use.

name: CAMP Tree Access Evo ANSI Replacement Bridge
keyword: camp tree access evo ansi replacement bridge
title: CAMP Tree Access Evo ANSI Replacement Bridge
h1: CAMP Tree Access Evo ANSI Replacement Bridge
meta: CAMP Tree Access Evo ANSI replacement bridge for your saddle. Swap a worn bridge on schedule and keep the saddle's main attachment point in service.
tagline: Replacement rope bridge for the CAMP Tree Access Evo ANSI saddle.
summary: This CAMP Tree Access Evo ANSI replacement bridge is the rope bridge for the Evo ANSI saddle. Bridges wear with every climb, so replacing them on schedule is part of keeping a saddle in service.
highlights: Made for the CAMP Tree Access Evo ANSI
Replaces a worn saddle bridge
Keeps your saddle in service
Factory part from CAMP

p: The bridge is where your climbing system attaches, and the ring or pulley on it runs back and forth all day. That wears the bridge faster than the rest of the saddle. Saddle makers design the bridge as a replaceable part so you can keep a good saddle going.
This bridge is made for the Tree Access Evo ANSI. Do not fit it to other saddles or use a bridge from another model.

The bridge also sets how your climbing system sits on your body. A fresh bridge at the correct length keeps the attachment point centered and positions the hitch and pulley where they work best, which makes long climbing days more comfortable.

Follow CAMP's instructions for length and fitting, and have a competent person check the work. Inspect the bridge before every climb for cuts, glazing, fuzzing or core showing, and replace it at the first sign of damage or when CAMP's guidance says to.
Saddles and bridges are life-support gear that should be used to ANSI Z133 and the maker's instructions. Find more saddle parts.
Keep a spare bridge with your kit so you can replace a worn one at the truck. Note the replacement date on your gear log so you know when the next one is due.

faq.q: Does this bridge fit other CAMP saddles?
faq.a: It is for the Tree Access Evo ANSI. Check CAMP's listing for other models.

faq.q: How do I know when to replace my saddle bridge?
faq.a: Replace it when the cover is worn, cut, glazed or shows the core, or when CAMP's guidance says it is due.

name: 3/4" Soft Anchor Rigging Sling
title: 3/4" Soft Anchor Rigging Sling for Heavy Rigging
meta: A 3/4" soft anchor rigging sling adjusts to the stem to hold blocks and lowering devices in place. Gentle on bark and sized for heavier rigging on removals.
tagline: Heavy 3/4 in adjustable rope sling for anchoring blocks and lowering devices.
summary: This 3/4 inch soft anchor rigging sling is an adjustable rope sling for anchoring rigging blocks and lowering devices. It wraps the stem, cinches to size and is easier on bark than chain.
highlights: 3/4 in rope for heavier rigging
Adjustable to fit different stem sizes
Soft on bark
Anchors blocks and lowering devices

p: Soft slings grip the stem and protect the bark compared with chain or wire. An adjustable sling cinches down to fit, so one sling covers a wide range of stem sizes. At 3/4 inch, this one is sized for heavier rigging where the block or lowering device is taking real force.
It also works at the base of the tree to anchor a port-a-wrap or other lowering device.

Rope slings have another benefit on heavy rigging: they can be choked tight and set on a stem with less slip than flat webbing, which helps keep a block exactly where you set it under shock load. They also store compactly in a rigging bag and can be paired with a second sling for redundancy when the job calls for it.
Check the rating on the tag before you rig, and remember that a dropped piece can load the system many times its weight. Make sure the anchor tree and every link in the system are sized for the load.
Inspect for cut strands, glazing, crushed sections or a pulled bury, and retire after heavy shock loading or damage. Keep it away from saw cuts. See other adjustable rigging slings.

faq.q: What size rigging is a 3/4 inch sling for?
faq.a: Heavier rigging, where the block or lowering device takes significant load. Check the rated capacity on the tag.

faq.q: Can I use it to anchor a lowering device?
faq.a: Yes. It works at the base of the tree to anchor a port-a-wrap or similar device.

name: Yale Beeline 8mm Loop Prusik with Aluminum Ring
title: Yale Beeline 8mm Loop Prusik with Aluminum Ring
h1: Yale Beeline 8mm Loop Prusik with Ring
meta: Yale Beeline 8mm loop prusik with an aluminum ring: a sewn polyester loop for adjusters, tool tethers and secondary hitches. Not a main hitch on big rope.
tagline: 8 mm Beeline polyester loop prusik with an aluminum ring.
summary: The Yale Beeline 8mm loop prusik is a polyester prusik loop with an aluminum ring attached. Climbers use it for lanyard adjusters, foot ascender backups and other secondary hitches.
highlights: 8 mm Yale Beeline polyester cord
Loop prusik with aluminum ring
For adjusters and secondary hitches
Firm, heat-resistant polyester

body.h: What an 8mm loop prusik is for
p: A prusik loop with a ring is a quick way to build an adjustable attachment: tie it around a rope, clip the ring and you have a grip that slides when unloaded and holds when loaded. Arborists use them as lanyard adjusters, foot ascender backups, or for tool and gear positioning.
At 8 mm it is smaller than a typical climbing hitch cord, so it grips well on thinner lines but should not be used as the main friction hitch on a full-size climbing rope unless the maker says so.

The aluminum ring gives a smooth, round attachment point for a carabiner or a micro pulley, and it keeps the hitch from wearing on a sharp connector. It also makes the loop easy to clip and unclip with gloves on when you are setting up at the base of the tree.
Test any hitch on the rope you will use it on before you trust it at height. Inspect the cord for glazing, fuzz, stiffness and cuts, and the ring for wear. Retire it at the first sign of damage.
Any life-support hitch must be used per Yale's instructions and ANSI Z133 by a trained climber. See all hitch cord and split tails.

faq.q: Can I use an 8mm prusik as my climbing hitch?
faq.a: Generally no. Use hitch cord sized and rated for your climbing rope. 8 mm loops are for adjusters and secondary uses.

faq.q: What is Yale Beeline made of?
faq.a: It is a polyester cord.

name: 10mm Beeline Polyester Sewn Eye-to-Eye Prusik
title: 10mm Beeline Eye-to-Eye Prusik, Sewn Polyester
meta: A 10mm Beeline eye-to-eye prusik in Yale polyester hitch cord, sewn for Distel and VT friction hitches. Firm, consistent cord for MRS and SRS climbing.
tagline: Sewn 10 mm Beeline polyester hitch cord for MRS and SRS hitches.
summary: This 10mm Beeline eye-to-eye prusik is Yale's polyester hitch cord with sewn eyes on both ends, ready to tie into a Distel or VT hitch. It is a popular choice for climbers on 11 to 13 mm lines.
highlights: 10 mm Yale Beeline polyester cord
Sewn eyes on both ends
Holds a Distel or VT well on common climbing lines
Firm hand for consistent hitch behavior

p: Beeline is a firm polyester hitch cord that holds its shape, so a hitch you dress today behaves the same tomorrow. Polyester also handles heat better than nylon, which matters when you descend steadily and the hitch warms up.
Sewn eyes make the hitch shorter and tidier than tied ends, leaving more room between hitch and pulley.

Many climbers pair a 10 mm hitch cord with 11 to 13 mm climbing lines because the slightly smaller cord grips well without being hard to tend. The sewn eyes are consistent, so when you replace the cord the new hitch behaves like the old one with little adjustment.
Always test a new hitch on your climbing rope low to the ground. The right number of wraps depends on your rope diameter and cover. Check that the climbing rope is in the range Yale recommends.
Inspect before every climb and replace when glazed, stiff, fuzzed through or when the stitching shows wear. Use per ANSI Z133 and Yale's instructions. See all eye-and-eye prusiks.
Keep a spare in the gear bag. A worn hitch cord can be swapped at the base of the tree in a few minutes, and it costs far less than the climbing rope it protects from heat and wear.

faq.q: What hitch should I tie with a 10mm Beeline eye-to-eye?
faq.a: Common choices are the Distel and VT. Use the hitch you are trained on and test before climbing.

faq.q: Is Beeline polyester or nylon?
faq.a: Polyester.

name: Petzl STRATO Upper Foam Replacement
title: Petzl STRATO Upper Foam Replacement Pad
meta: Petzl STRATO upper foam replacement pad. Swap worn or dirty foam to keep your helmet comfortable and fitted, and recheck fit with ear muffs after the swap.
tagline: Replacement upper comfort foam for Petzl STRATO helmets.
summary: This Petzl STRATO upper foam replacement swaps out the comfort foam in a STRATO helmet. Sweat and grime wear foam out long before the shell, and fresh foam keeps the helmet fitting the way it should.
highlights: Replacement upper foam for Petzl STRATO
Restores comfort and fit
Easy swap, no tools
Cheaper than a new helmet

p: A helmet you wear every day collects sweat, sawdust and sunscreen. The foam pads compress, get smelly and stop holding the helmet where it should sit. Fresh foam brings back comfort and stops the helmet from shifting, which matters when you add ear muffs or a visor.
It is a simple fix that keeps a good helmet in service.

It also helps with hygiene. Helmets get passed between climbers on some crews, and fresh foam is an easy way to keep a shared helmet clean. Many climbers keep a spare set so they can wash one while wearing the other.

Remove the old foam, clean the inside of the shell with mild soap and water, and press the new foam into place as Petzl shows. Check the helmet fit and chin strap after the swap, and make sure your muffs still seal against your head; see our hearing protection if you need new muffs.
Replacing foam does not extend a helmet's service life. Retire the helmet after an impact or per Petzl's lifespan guidance, and inspect the shell and headband regularly.
Keep the old foam out of the bin until the new set is seated and the helmet fits right, so you can compare thickness and placement if anything feels off.

faq.q: Will this foam fit any Petzl helmet?
faq.a: It is made for the STRATO range. Check your model before ordering.

faq.q: How often should I replace helmet foam?
faq.a: When it is compressed, damaged or will not come clean. Daily users often replace it every season.

name: Edelrid Talon Replacement Gaffs
title: Edelrid Talon Replacement Gaffs for Climbing Spurs
meta: Edelrid Talon replacement gaffs swap out worn or damaged points on your Talon climbing spurs and keep them biting cleanly. Fit and file to the maker's guide.
tagline: Replacement gaffs that keep Edelrid Talon spurs biting cleanly.
summary: These Edelrid Talon replacement gaffs fit Talon climbing spurs. Gaffs wear down and get damaged with use, and swapping them is how you keep the spurs safe and biting on removals.
highlights: Made for Edelrid Talon spurs
Replaces worn or damaged gaffs
Restores clean bite in bark
Swap instead of replacing the whole spur

p: A gaff that is too short, bent, chipped or sharpened the wrong way can cut out of the tree, and a gaff cut-out is a serious hazard. Check gaff length and profile against Edelrid's guidance and replace when they are worn past the limit or damaged.
Spurs are for removals and emergency access only. Do not spike trees you are pruning.

Talon spurs are designed with replaceable gaffs so climbers can keep the same spur frame and pads while swapping the part that wears. That saves money over replacing the whole spur, and it lets you keep the fit you are used to.

Fit the gaffs following Edelrid's instructions and torque any hardware as specified. Sharpen only by hand file on the outside faces as the maker describes; grinding changes the profile and can overheat the steel.
Use gaff guards whenever the spurs are off the tree. Spurs and gaffs should be used by trained climbers as part of a system that meets ANSI Z133. Find more replacement gaffs and parts.
Check the gaffs every time you put the spurs on: look for chips, bends and length. Measure them against Edelrid's minimum and swap before they reach it rather than after.

faq.q: Do these gaffs fit other spurs?
faq.a: They are made for Edelrid Talon spurs.

faq.q: How should I sharpen Talon gaffs?
faq.a: By hand file on the outside faces as Edelrid describes. Do not grind.

name: ArborTec Cobra DryKit Rope Bag (65L)
title: ArborTec Cobra DryKit Rope Bag 65L
meta: The ArborTec Cobra DryKit 65L rope bag keeps climbing rope and gear dry and clean in the truck and on site. A roomy dry bag for ropes, saddles and kit.
tagline: 65 liter dry bag for ropes and climbing kit in wet weather.
summary: The ArborTec Cobra DryKit rope bag holds 65 liters of rope and gear and keeps it dry and clean. It is a good fit for a climbing line plus a saddle and hardware.
highlights: 65 L capacity
Dry bag construction for wet days
Keeps rope and gear clean
Fits a climbing line plus kit

p: Rope and soft gear last longer when kept clean and dry. A wet rope dragged across a muddy site picks up grit that cuts fibers from the inside. A dry bag keeps rope, saddle and hardware out of rain, mud, sawdust and the fuel and oil in the truck bed.
At 65 liters there is space for a climbing line and the rest of your kit in one bag.

A roomy dry bag also makes the start of each job faster. Instead of pulling separate pieces from the truck, the climber grabs one bag with rope, saddle and hardware together. On wet days, the gear starts the climb dry instead of soaked from the truck bed.
Let wet gear dry fully before sealing it in, since trapped moisture can lead to mildew. Keep the bag away from saw chain and sharp tools. Wipe out sawdust and grit regularly.
Inspect your rope and gear after removing it from the bag, as always. Browse other gear bags.
Store the bag out of direct sun when not in use, and check seams and closures for wear. A bag that no longer seals will still carry gear but will not keep it dry.

faq.q: How much does the Cobra DryKit hold?
faq.a: 65 liters.

faq.q: Can I store wet rope in it?
faq.a: Dry it first. Sealing in a wet rope can cause mildew.

name: Teufelberger Fresh Swell Climbing Long Sleeve T-Shirt
title: Teufelberger Fresh Swell Long Sleeve Climbing Shirt
h1: Teufelberger Fresh Swell Long Sleeve T-Shirt
meta: The Teufelberger Fresh Swell long sleeve climbing t-shirt is a work shirt for climbers who want arm coverage in the tree. Comfortable for long days aloft.
tagline: Long sleeve climbing shirt from Teufelberger for days in the tree.
summary: The Teufelberger Fresh Swell long sleeve climbing t-shirt gives arm coverage against bark, sun and bugs. It is a comfortable layer for a long climbing day.
highlights: Long sleeves for arm coverage
Teufelberger climbing apparel
Comfortable under a harness
Good for sun and bark protection

p: Bark scrapes, sun, poison ivy and bugs all argue for covering your arms in the tree. A long sleeve shirt gives that coverage and is easy to layer under a jacket on cold mornings.
A shirt that fits close but moves freely is easier to work in than a loose one that catches on limbs.

Teufelberger is best known for climbing and rigging rope, and the Fresh Swell shirt carries its name for climbers who want a shirt from a brand they already trust. A comfortable layer matters on long days aloft, when you are in the saddle for hours and moving through tight canopy.
Check the sizing chart before ordering. Wash cold and line dry to keep the fit. Clothing is not PPE; wear chainsaw protection, eye and hearing protection and a helmet as the job calls for.
See our full clothing range for pants, boots and outer layers.

Many climbers keep two or three work shirts in rotation so there is always a clean one ready for the next day. A long sleeve shirt is also a good base layer under a work jacket or high-visibility vest when the weather turns cold. Bright colors also help ground crew keep track of the climber in the canopy.

faq.q: Is the Fresh Swell shirt protective gear?
faq.a: No. It is a work shirt. Wear proper PPE for the task.

faq.q: How should I wash it?
faq.a: Wash cold and line dry.

name: Husqvarna Vibration Damper for 395XP
title: Husqvarna Vibration Damper for 395XP Chainsaws
meta: Replacement Husqvarna vibration damper for the 395XP chainsaw. Swap worn dampers to cut vibration, steady the handle and save your hands on long workdays.
tagline: Replacement anti-vibration damper for the Husqvarna 395XP.
summary: This Husqvarna vibration damper fits the 395XP chainsaw. Worn dampers let more vibration into your hands and make the saw feel loose, so replacing them keeps a big saw comfortable and controllable.
highlights: Fits Husqvarna 395XP
Restores anti-vibration performance
Steadies the handle against the powerhead
Protects hands on long bucking days

p: The 395XP is a big saw used for long bucking and felling sessions. Its anti-vibration system relies on dampers between the handle and powerhead. When they wear, crack or sag, you feel more buzz in your hands and the handle feels loose or rattles.
Long-term vibration exposure is linked to hand and arm problems, so worn dampers are worth replacing promptly.

Dampers are rubber or spring parts, and rubber breaks down over time with heat, fuel and oil. On a saw that runs every day, it is normal for dampers to need replacing before the engine needs major work. Swapping them is much cheaper than dealing with a loose handle that cracks or a saw that is tiring to use.
Check which damper position you need, since saws often use different dampers in different places. Replace in sets if several are worn. If you are not sure, have a dealer do the job.
Always run the saw with chaps, eye and hearing protection and a helmet. See other power equipment parts.

After fitting, check that the handle is secure and that there is no metal-to-metal contact between the handle and powerhead. Start the saw and feel for unusual vibration before taking it back to work.

faq.q: Does this damper fit the 395XP?
faq.a: Yes. It is listed for the 395XP. Check the position you need before ordering.

faq.q: How do I know my dampers are worn?
faq.a: More hand vibration, a loose or rattling handle, or cracked rubber are common signs.
